test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 4 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a basic assumption of one-way ANOVA?

options.text: k samples have approximately unequal variances
Error terms eᵢj are independently and identically distributed as normal with mean zero and variance σe².

solution:
The correct answer is **k samples have approximately unequal variances.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The basic assumptions of one-way ANOVA are as follows: 

 
 
• The error terms (residuals) are independently and identically distributed as normal with mean zero and constant variance (homoscedasticity).
 
• The dependent variable is quantitative and continuous.
 
• The various effects, such as the group means, follow additivity.
 
• The observations within each group are independent of each other.
 
 
 
• **Error terms eij are independently and identically distributed as normal with mean zero and variance σe²:**
 
 
• This assumption states that the error terms (residuals) in each group are normally distributed with a mean of zero and constant variance (homoscedasticity). It also assumes that the errors are independent, meaning that the error in one observation is not related to the errors in other observations.
 
 
 
• **The dependent variable is quantitative: **
 
 
• **​**This assumption states that the dependent variable being analyzed in the one-way ANOVA is a quantitative variable, typically measured on a continuous scale. The ANOVA is not suitable for categorical or ordinal variables.
 
 
 
• **Various effects follow additivity:**
 
 
• This assumption states that the effects of different factors in the model, such as the group means or treatment effects, are additive. In other words, the overall effect of a combination of factors can be obtained by adding the individual effects of each factor.
 
 

 
• k samples have approximately unequal variances: 

 
 
• It states that the k samples have approximately unequal variances. However, this assumption is not a basic assumption of one-way ANOVA. Instead, the basic assumption is that the variances within each group are approximately equal (homoscedasticity). Unequal variances can cause issues with the validity of ANOVA results. 
 
 

Hence, this is not a basic assumption of one-way ANOVA.
